notes.subject: other
notes.text: Drives on the left, unlike its mainland neighbours Cambodia and Laos.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Large white plates on private cars and yellow plates on commercial vehicles; yellow commercial plates are unique in the region.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Square bollard with a pointed top and black-and-white stripes.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bulky square white sign posts, often with the bottom painted black; unique in the region.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Square concrete poles with small holes running up them.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Concrete roads with a large square slab pattern are common.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Compact script whose letters mostly contain tiny circles; Khmer has longer lines and more marks below the letters.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow centre lines, solid or dashed.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Street light poles have red-and-black or black-and-white stripes at the base, and long thin lamp arms hang over the road.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Small-road direction signs come as two stacked white panels; highway signs are green with Latin text under the local script.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs use local script instead of Latin letters.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Road markers with a Garuda: white on national roads, black on provincial roads.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Streets are often lined with flags, including yellow royal flags.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Distinctive green village signs that exist in no other country.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Most Generation 3 coverage shows no car at all.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat dry plains in the middle and east, tall mountains in the northwest and exposed-rock mountains in the west and south.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: National roads starting with 1 are north, 2 northeast, 3 centre and 4 south.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Landline area codes: the capital uses 02 and others use three digits; mobile numbers start 08 or 09.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Provincial road waystones show a two-letter province abbreviation in the local script.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The far south shows mosques, Islamic attire and Jawi script on signs.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Rubber plantations with small black taps on trunks and oil palm plantations are mostly in the south.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Red songthaew pickup taxis are most common in the northern city of Chiang Mai.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Teak trees and Tenasserim pines are mostly in the north and northwest.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A touristy, wealthy island with modern buildings, resorts and heavy traffic among hills.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Helm-shaped street signs exist only in one resort city.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Pink and yellow-on-green taxis; pink ones are practically exclusive to the capital.
